record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: If the curvature curv_R(M) of a finitely generated graded R-module M is greater than 1, does there exist a real constant a such that b_i^R(M)/(curv_R(M))^i converges to a as i tends to infinity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $R = \bigoplus_{n\ge 0} R_n$ be a standard graded Noetherian $k$-algebra over a field $k = R_0$, and let $M$ be a finitely generated graded $R$-module. Denote by $b_i^R(M) = \dim_k \operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M,k)$ the $i$-th graded Betti number of $M$, and define the curvature of $M$ by
$$\operatorname{curv}_R(M) = \limsup_{i\to\infty} \big(b_i^R(M)\big)^{1/i}.$$
Suppose $\operatorname{curv}_R(M) > 1$. Does there exist a real constant $a$ (depending on $R$ and $M$) such that
$$\lim_{i\to\infty} \frac{b_i^R(M)}{\operatorname{curv}_R(M)^i} = a\, ?$$
artifact.category_tag: Asymptotic Betti numbers and curvature of modules
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns Avramov-style homological curvature of finitely generated graded modules and the precise asymptotic growth rate of Betti numbers. Recent work (e.g., 2024 papers on complexity and curvature of Cohen-Macaulay modules) discusses these invariants and provides only limsup-type bounds; no proof or counterexample to the convergence of $b_i^R(M)/\operatorname{curv}_R(M)^i$ when $\operatorname{curv}_R(M)>1$ appears in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Complexity and curvature of (pairs of) Cohen-Macaulay modules
status_evidence.snippet: The complexity and curvature of a module, introduced by Avramov, measure the growth of Betti and Bass numbers of a module.
status_evidence.claim: Curvature of modules is an active research invariant; precise asymptotics remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Modules with extremal resolutions (Avramov)
status_evidence.snippet: Homological curvatures discriminate among modules with infinite complexities; the projective curvature is defined by a limsup of Betti numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Curvature is defined as a limsup; convergence of normalized Betti numbers is not established in general.
